sections.html:
Parker is a home rule town in northeastern Douglas County, about 23 miles southeast of downtown Denver. Castle Rock, the county seat, is about 15 miles to the southwest, and the city of Aurora touches Parker's northeast border.

Cherry Creek flows through town on its way north to Denver. Unincorporated communities that border Parker include Dove Valley, Stonegate and The Pinery. The town sits at roughly 5,834 feet and is the second most populous town in Douglas County after Castle Rock.

Parker's growth is unusual even by Front Range standards. The town had 285 people when it incorporated in 1981. By 2014 about 48,000 lived there, and the 2020 census counted 58,512. Census figures show 5,450 residents in 1990, 23,558 in 2000 and 45,297 in 2010.

Much of that growth came in the mid-1990s and mid-2000s as Denver's southern suburbs spread. Because so many Parker homes date from those two waves, a large share are now between roughly 20 and 30 years old, an age when roofs, water heaters and original appliances come due.

The age profile reflects the building boom: the 2020 median age was 35.9, 27.5 percent of residents were under 18 and only 9.3 percent were 65 or older. Parker calls itself a town under the state's home rule statutes, and the sales tax rate is listed at 8.0 percent.

Household makeup tells the same story. In 2020, 60.3 percent of households were married-couple households and 42.4 percent had children under 18.

The area's earliest known residents were ancient Plains Woodland peoples, followed by Utes, Arapaho and Cheyenne. In 1864 Alfred Butters opened the Pine Grove Way Station, a one-room stop for travelers. It was later moved to Main Street and expanded into the Twenty Mile House, named for its distance from Denver.

James S. Parker, a Civil War veteran from Illinois, bought the station in 1870, added a blacksmith shop and mercantile and served as postmaster. The settlement was renamed Parker in 1882, the year the Denver and New Orleans Railroad arrived. The Parker station closed in 1931.

The Parker City Land Company began a planned western town in the 1960s but ran short of money, and another builder finished the work around 1980 or 1981. Parker incorporated on May 1, 1981. Victorian-style houses were built along Pikes Peak Drive in the 1910s. Historic sites in town include the Twenty Mile post office building, the Ruth Memorial Methodist Episcopal Church and the Hood House.

sections.h2: What are Parker's climate and flood history?
sections.html:
Parker has a semi-arid climate that is classed as BSk, a mid-latitude steppe type with large year-to-year swings in precipitation. The town sits at roughly 5,900 feet above sea level.

Local history includes the flood of Tallman Gulch in 1912, in which the Hood House was one of two houses that sustained no damage. The house now stands in Preservation Park.

Homes near Cherry Creek or a gulch deserve a quick floodplain check, and so does any basement that has taken on water. Colorado also reappraises real property every two years in odd-numbered years, so a valuation notice arrives in the spring of those years.

sections.h2: Which schools and services are in Parker?
sections.html:
Parker is served by the Douglas County School District. Public high schools in the area are Legend, Ponderosa and Chaparral. There are also six public charter schools and several private schools, including Ave Maria Catholic School and Lutheran High School Parker.

  • Arapahoe Community College has a Parker campus.
  • Rocky Vista University College of Osteopathic Medicine is in Parker.
  • AdventHealth Parker is the town's only hospital.
  • The Parker Arts, Culture and Events Center hosts exhibits, theater and concerts.

Check school boundaries with the district itself rather than relying on a sales description.

sections.h2: What parks, trails and water features does Parker have?
sections.html:
The town maintains 10 trails with more than 27 miles of paved multi-use paths, over 6 miles of natural-surface equestrian trails and a 1.8-mile loop. It has about 250 acres of developed parkland and more than 900 acres of open space. The Cherry Creek Trail follows the creek through town.

West of town is Rueter-Hess Reservoir. It is fed by water rights held by the Parker Water and Sanitation District, delivered through Cherry Creek and local canals, and if filled to capacity it would cover 1,140 acres. As of 2021, the water itself was not open for recreation, though trails around it were.

Recreation facilities include the Parker Recreation Center, the Parker Field House with 100,000 square feet of space and the Parker Racquet Club, which opened in 2019.

sections.h2: When are Douglas County property taxes due for a Parker home?
sections.html:
Douglas County sets the first-half payment for the last day of February, the second half for June 15 and the full payment for April 30. If a date falls on a weekend, the deadline moves to the next business day.

The county mails statements or postcard notices in January and posts them online at its tax site. It says it does not bill mortgage lenders, and that not receiving a statement does not excuse a taxpayer from paying, citing C.R.S. 39-10-103(1)(a). If a second payment for the first half is received, the overage is applied to the second half, and refunds happen only when taxes are paid in full.

Many Parker owners have a lender that pays through escrow, but the county does not bill that lender directly. If you are selling a house with a mortgage, confirm with your servicer that the tax was paid and ask what happens to any escrow balance after payoff.

sections.h2: What should you know about Colorado transfer fees and recording?
sections.html:
Colorado's state documentary fee is 1 cent per $100 on a transfer with consideration above $500, according to Weld County's recording guidance, which cites state law. That applies across counties, including Douglas.

  • A deed must show the grantee's mailing address so tax statements go to the new owner.
  • Recorded documents are public, so leave out personal identifiers such as Social Security numbers.
  • Recording fees are set by statute and must be paid when documents are submitted.
  • The recorder can refuse documents that do not meet margin standards.

Recording happens in the county where the property sits, so confirm local procedure with the title company handling your closing.

sections.h2: How do Parker sellers weigh a listing against a cash sale?
sections.html:
Parker's median household income was $120,075 in the 2022 survey, and a well-kept house will draw buyers who can finance. A house with deferred repairs, a difficult tenant or an inherited title is harder to list well.

If that describes your situation, a cash purchase as-is can be worth a look. Tell us about the house, the timeline and any liens, and we will explain how the process would work for that property before you decide.
